- If sentiment is positive (≥ 0.25) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- If sentiment is negative (≤ -0.25) in recent days, model tends to underestimate; increase forecast slightly.
- After a sharp price spike, model often overshoots in the next 5–10 days; apply a downward correction of 1–3%.
- Model frequently overestimates mean-reversion targets; if recent history shows strong trend, adjust forecast to align with 3–5 day moving average.
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture late-period volatility; add a 1–2% downward bias if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- If sentiment history shows a sudden shift from neutral to positive, model may lag; adjust forecast to reflect sentiment change within 2–3 days.
